title: The Unwritten Benchmark: A New Challenge for Multimodal Machine Learning in Abstract Perceptual Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.14558v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Current multimodal models have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in recognizing static visual and auditory content. However, their capacity for abstract perceptual reasoning, inferring unseen information from dynamic, generative processes, remains a critical and underexplored frontier. In this paper, we introduce The Unwritten Benchmark, a new challenge designed to probe this abstract perceptual and cognitive ability. We define the core task as acousto-kinematic word inference: models must decipher words, across 3 different writing styles, being written solely from the audio of pen scratches and the video of hand movements, without any visible ink trace. Our evaluation results reveal a profound gap between human and machine performance: while human participants achieve high ordered letter accuracy (over 80%), leading Multimodal Machine Learning Models, including GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5-Pro, struggle significantly, failing to surpass 10%.

translated_title: 未书写的基准：多模态机器学习在抽象感知推理中的新挑战
translated_abstract: 当前的多模态模型在识别静态视觉和听觉内容方面表现出显著能力。然而，它们在抽象感知推理——从动态、生成过程中推断未见信息——方面的能力，仍然是一个关键且未被充分探索的前沿。在本文中，我们引入了“未书写的基准”，这是一个旨在探索这种抽象感知和认知能力的新挑战。我们将核心任务定义为声学-运动学词汇推断：模型必须破译单词，涵盖3种不同的书写风格，这些单词仅通过笔划的音频和手部运动的视频来书写，而没有任何可见的墨迹痕迹。我们的评估结果揭示了人类与机器性能之间的深刻差距：虽然人类参与者实现了较高的字母顺序准确率（超过80%），但领先的多模态机器学习模型，包括GPT-4o和Gemini 2.5-Pro，却表现艰难，未能超过10%。
tldr: 本文提出“未书写基准”，要求模型仅从笔声和手部动作推断书写单词，发现人类准确率超80%，而最先进的多模态模型如GPT-4o和Gemini 2.5-Pro不足10%，凸显抽象感知推理的显著差距。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Unwritten Benchmark, requiring models to infer written words solely from pen sounds and hand movements, revealing that humans achieve over 80% accuracy while top multimodal models like GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5-Pro fall below 10%, highlighting a major gap in abstract perceptual reasoning.
